description: The figure shows two multi-level (sunburst-style) pie charts comparing the distribution of document categories (inner ring: broad domains; outer ring: subcategories) for two datasets/classifications, with the right chart titled “FineWeb-Edu Classifier.” Each chart contains 5 inner-ring slices and multiple outer-ring slices labeled with counts (not percentages), and both use consistent domain colors (green for Education, blue for Health & Medicine, red for Science, orange for History & Society, and brown for Tech & Engineering), with outer slices in related shades; labels are placed on or outside slices with leader lines, and there is no separate legend. In the left chart, the inner ring shows Education 25 (green), Health & Medicine 22 (blue), History & Society 23 (orange), Science 15 (red), and Tech & Engineering 12 (brown); the outer ring breaks these into Teaching & resources 15 and Science & technology education 10 (Education), Diseases 11, Medical 6, and Nutrition 5 (Health & Medicine), Animal & Plant 13 and Materials 2 (Science), Historical review 7, Society & culture 10, and Events & people 6 (History & Society), and Infor tech 5, Materials 3, Emerging tech 4, Manage 2, and Policy 1 (Tech & Engineering). In the right chart (“FineWeb-Edu Classifier”), the inner ring shows Education 38 (green), Health & Medicine 19 (blue), History & Society 19 (orange), Science 15 (red), and Tech & Engineering 8 (brown); the outer ring shows Teaching & resources 17, Science & technology education 19, and Healthy education 2 (Education), Diseases 10, Nutrition 7, and Medical 2 (Health & Medicine), Animal & Plant 12 and Materials 3 (Science), Historical review 12, Society & culture 5, and Events & people 2 (History & Society), and Infor tech 3, Materials 1, Emerging tech 4, and Manage 1 (Tech & Engineering). Several slices on the right chart appear visually emphasized by being slightly offset/exploded (notably the large green Education sector and some adjacent slices), and the slice ordering appears arranged around the circle by domain groupings rather than strictly by descending size.
